content: Nifedipine is prescribed for the management of vasospastic angina, which is confirmed by one or more of the following criteria: 1. The presence of a classical pattern of angina occurring at rest, accompanied by ST-segment elevation on an electrocardiogram. 2. Angina or coronary artery spasm that is provoked by the administration of ergonovine. 3. Coronary artery spasm that is demonstrated through angiographic imaging. In patients who have undergone angiography, the diagnosis of vasospastic angina is not excluded by the presence of significant fixed obstructive coronary artery disease, as long as the above criteria are met. This includes cases where the pain threshold varies with exertion, in unstable angina with electrocardiographic findings consistent with intermittent vasospasm, or when angina is resistant to treatment with nitrates and/or adequate doses of beta-blockers. Nifedipine is also indicated for the management of chronic stable angina (effort-associated angina) in patients who do not exhibit evidence of vasospasm. It is used in cases where symptoms persist despite adequate treatment with beta-blockers and/or organic nitrates, or in patients who cannot tolerate these medications. In clinical trials lasting up to eight weeks, nifedipine has been shown to reduce the frequency of angina episodes and improve exercise tolerance in patients with chronic stable angina. However, the long-term safety and sustained effectiveness of nifedipine in these patients have not been fully established. Limited studies involving small patient populations suggest that the combined use of nifedipine and beta-blockers may be beneficial for managing chronic stable angina. However, the available data is insufficient to reliably predict the effects of this combination therapy, particularly in patients with compromised left ventricular function or cardiac conduction abnormalities. When initiating such combination therapy, it is essential to closely monitor blood pressure, as the combined effects of these drugs can lead to severe hypotension. (Refer to the WARNINGS section for further details.) Nifedipine extended-release tablets are also indicated for the treatment of hypertension. They can be used as monotherapy or in combination with other antihypertensive agents.
